First and foremost I'm a life long and very absorbed student of weapons and war - both by education and passion. For absolute breadth there is no game like it and it's absorbed me for countless hours. It's an addictive hobby, but no more so than most others military history nuts come into. The vehicles are amazing and it's a gorgeous game. For sheer cinematic value on average hardware nothing can beat it.

That said War Thunder is far from perfect - the attention to crafting the vehicles and weapons is immersive. The battlefields might as well come from Star Fox or Battletech and the community can be more than a little toxic as it includes a lot of youngsters with out any supervision. 

Arcade mode is just that, and can be a blast - air arcade has some of the most imaginative battlefields and landscapes out there but it's also nuts and you have to just laugh when you get taken out. Ground arcade is just a simplified mode of ground 'Real Battle' with easier aiming and quicker game play. For old eyes like mine it's a go to. If you're not someone who needs a million miles a minute and can cope with slower gameplay, Naval is awesome - and some of the extended conflict matches (bigger maps ~ 2hr games, but you can duck out whenever) are the best game modes War Thunder devs have ever made. Depending on the state of the game it's possible for opposing spawn points (your choice to spawn there) to occur with in less than 5km of one another. For battleships this can be a thrilling point blank 'broadside' fight that is as much a test of fortitude as it is skill.

Calling a mode 'Real Battle' is a bit of a farce as well - air consists of a map for ~ 60 aircraft, 30 per side, lined up at 70km distance for jets, and a line of 'ground targets' (very simple firebases)  There are 'supply bases' that can be bombed, but both Air Arcade and air 'RB' are filled with dogfight obsessed players, many of whom cannot comprehend why aircraft are included (now to include strategic bombers) that cannot dogfight. High tier featuring many of the slick, modern aircraft featured in promos is nothing but 'missile spam.' Missiles begin flying like a medieval arrow storm at anywhere from 50km on in, and though some claim one can be skilled enough to avoid or dodge (and there is much insulting and name-calling if one cannot dodge how other players think it should be done.) At lower levels air RB can be fun but it gets repetitive. You have no choice of what map you're flying in and you must have your battle lineup selected before time. There is less focus on fighters only but bombers almost always fly alone as there is no real insentive to do otherwise. 

As a matter of fact there is no real reason to play the game according to militarily accurate tactics at all. Other than a voice comms linked group of up to four can utterly dominate air or ground if the players are adequate and good at covering one another. People from some areas in the world are accused at length of cheating because their gaming culture is competitive and collaborative - there are highly developed 'clans' or squadrons that have extremely well thought out and coordinated 'battle nets' allowing even randomly spawned 'allies' to coordinate and work efficiently. For lone wolf players this can be frustrating to the point of infuriating and cause...again...toxic behavior and words of team chat.

Sim is the 'redheaded stepchild' of War Thunder and only Air Sim is worth mentioning. Play is strictly first person (from the cockpit) and the maps range from 64 x 64km to 128 x 128km. Battles are long, and there is bigger balance between strike & bomber players, and fighter pilots. Flight models can vary radically from RB and often planes that are dogs in that mode shine in Sim. 90% of content creators, especially those famous for rating vehicles, ignore this mode as the younger crowd looking for short games considers it 'boring.' For the most part the sim community is small enough that you get to know other regular players - the best part being you aren't restricted to a random map and bunch of players. If you don't like a particular map, choose another. If you find someone you detest in the lobby, go to another one. 

Gaijin, War Thunder's developer, has a very puzzling if straight forward business model...and they also listen way too much to 'the mob' on their forums. Besides their ability to take any new game mode and ruin it: a new 'nuclear escalation' mode is populated by respawning and rage-inducingly accurate SAM sites that are very difficult to eliminate thanks to a unrealistic mechanic where something like 90% of the weapons launched at them are successfully intercepted. One of the main marketing tools is 'snail rage' (Gaijin's logo is a snail) where players end up so angry at the game they either uninstall...or buy a premium vehicle. Which used to help for a while as they tend to be more powerful, but not so much anymore. 

Further, today's 'top gun' will eventually get either raised in battle rating so it's operating against far tougher (to the point of invulnerable) opponents or have weapons 'nerfed.' Always claiming some new data, game devs routinely take a weapons system that preforms reliably better than others and make it worse. Sometimes it's because the hue and cry of the mob of players (most who are young and often toxic) sometimes it's to sell a new premium vehicle.

Last, a word of advice: Free to Play is wholly misleading. Some players pride themselves on climbing the ranks with out paying a dime. They cry about 'pay to win' players but often this is because they don't have a job and don't comprehend that the game is developed as a business. For those playing in places with depressed economies, there is no scaling of costs however and for someone somewhere else in the world paying $80 for a premium vehicle is insane, where as here it's less than a day's wages.
